newsitem.title: USA: Alaskan agency to aid seafood processing plant.
newsitem.headline: Alaskan agency to aid seafood processing plant.

text.p: With visions of Alaskans producing 100 million pounds of seafood product a year, a state board voted on Tuesday to advance $10 million to encourage the $120 million project.

The Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority (AIDEA) approved the financing for the center, a proposed 184,000-square-foot facility in Anchorage that could employ 450 people, state officials said.
It would have the capacity to produce 100 million pounds annually of prepared seafood product from raw pollock, cod, salmon, halibut and flatfish, officials said.
"We are pleased we can approve initial financing assistance to keep the developer's plans on track," Wilson Hughes, AIDEA board chairman, said in a statement.
The financing is contingent on the developers' securing a letter of credit, AIDEA said.
The Anchorage-based developers want a $50 million loan from AIDEA, coupled with financing from a Taiwanese company, to establish what they call the "Alaska Seafood Center."
The AIDEA board, which in March approved up to $1 million for project review, is expected to consider the full loan later this summer, officials said.
AIDEA in 1993 was granted legislative approval to loan up to $50 million for such a seafood-processing center. The loan would be repaid through lease payments, AIDEA said.
